blockers: Abstract (paper/main.tex:19) says 'within each source, the pooled format added false choices on problems the judge could not solve and not on problems it solved', and main.tex:30 and :67 say the direction is 'consistent across sources' / 'the same within each source'. Recomputed from raw, the third source (arXiv-derived C2 replication set) points the other way: solved n=4, PICK-ISO +0.50 [0.00,+1.00]; unsolved n=74, +0.135 [+0.03,+0.24] (exps/posthoc/solvability_by_source.json agrees). The paper's sb_* macros list only the screen and contest sets and omit this stratum. The claim is false as worded for 1 of 3 sources and it is the paper's only substantive exploratory finding. Reword to 'two of three sources, the third has only 4 solved problems', or report all six strata.

Solve (repo parser/grader): S1 36/60, contest 17/24=0.708, arXiv 4/78=0.051, union 21/102=0.206 (1 missing). Posthoc split reproduces: solved n=57 D -0.070 [-0.19,+0.05]; unsolved n=105 +0.133 [+0.05,+0.22]. Unsolved-minus-solved difference +0.20 [+0.06,+0.35], but it is pooled across sources and solvability is almost collinear with source (arXiv: 74 of 78 unsolved; contest: 17 of 24 solved). Within source the unsolved intervals include or touch 0 (screen [-0.04,+0.29]; contest [0.00,+0.43], n=7). Post hoc, one SOLVE attempt per problem (regression to the mean in the split). The paper hedges this correctly; the 'penalty depends on competence' wording in contribution (2) is stronger than this evidence.

H2 on the gated contest set (+0.125, p about 0.04, unadjusted, not significant after Holm over 4 tests) rests on 3 of 24 problems with a nonzero difference, all positive, 21 exactly zero. The abstract's 'the wrong candidate a forced choice selects is the one verification passes most' is also from the union (p 0.0013), which ruling A2 declared uninterpretable. The mechanism reading (selection then verification) is also confounded with candidate plausibility (the forced pick is the most plausible candidate, which any later check would favour). Keep it as exploratory.

A2 (gate conflict ruling) was made after seeing data and after round-1 review; it is disclosed, and both readings are reported. The preregistration itself does not decide the conflict, so this is a deviation of interpretation, not a hidden one. Sonnet cap overrun (29.10 vs 12 USD, D3) and the blocked call (D1) are disclosed.

Complete-case handling: sonnet H1 n=17 of 24 (6 PICK missing/unparsed, 5 ISO unparsed) and H2 n=19; posthoc/solvability_split.py silently drops pools with unparseable PICK/ISO. For haiku nothing is dropped (0 unparsed in 103 + 60 pools), so no effect on headline numbers.

Unit and structural asymmetry: problem is the unit (TA pools one per problem; OK). ISO-any uses 3 calls vs 1 PICK call, which biases D downward, so a positive D is conservative but the equivalence test is biased toward showing equivalence; main.tex:84 mentions the call counts only briefly.

Multiplicity: results/hypothesis_ledger.csv now has 64 rows; results.tex ledger_total says 61 (stale; three later rows for A2 and the by-source posthoc were added). Preregistered Holm covers 4 tests only; 15+ screen CIs are unadjusted and reported as exploratory, which is appropriate. Contest-set power is low by the preregistration's own statement (half-width 0.125).

Section title 'Screen: no lineup penalty on problems the judge mostly solves' (main.tex:54) is about the screen (D -0.033 [-0.15,+0.083], n=60); fine as a screen result, but equivalence at 0.10 was not shown there either (lower bound -0.15).
